we present the first provably robust constrained reinforcement learning algorithm that is able to learn policies that maximize future rewards in the presence of model misspecification, while also ensuring that constraints are not violated, and we demonstrate its effectiveness in multiple challenging continuous control domains.

we present a robust constrained RL method that can learn policies for physical control tasks with model misspecification that can satisfy constraints and perform better than existing methods in a variety of domains.

we develop a new method for constrained reinforcement learning that is robust to model misspecification, we show that this method can outperform existing state-of-the-art methods on the RWRL benchmark, and we provide an analysis of the method's performance on a range of Mujoco tasks from this benchmark.

the following questions: How can we learn a robust policy that maximizes expected reward in a perturbed environment, and satisfies constraints, even if the perturbations are unknown? How can we learn robust policies that are robust with respect to a large class of model misspecification, without having to explicitly specify the perturbation class?
